To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have identified the mutation spectrum of the TY and SLC45 A2 gene in patients with o culocutaneous al binism.
the TYR gene mutations are the most common cause of OCA1 in Korea, and that OCA4 is also present in Korean OCA families.
6 distinct mutations in the TYR gene were identified in 15 of the 16 alleles, and a novel missense mutation in SLC45A 2 was detected in a Korean OCA patient.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis of OCA in Korea.
the molecular analysis of the TYR gene in 12 Korean OCA patients.
the molecular genetic analysis of the TYR gene and SLC45 A2 gene in Korean patients with OCA.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the majority of Korean OCA patients have TYR gene mutations.
OCA4 is not common in Korea.
OCA1 is the most common form, followed by OCA4.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Korean population has a higher frequency of OCA1 than OCA4.
8 of 10 (80%) Korean OCA patients were found to have OCA1, and the other 2 (20%) patients had OCA4.
the TYR mutations were more common in the Korean OCA patients than those of the SLC45 A2 mutations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the most frequent mutation in OCA1 in Koreans is the same as that found in Japanese and Han Chinese, which is c.929insCT.
the TYR and the SLC45a2 genes are the main genes associated with oculocoutaneous albinism.
c.929ins C is the most common mutation in the Korean OCA1 population.
